title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TANYA'S BRIDGE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tanya Briggs, a drawbridge operator in Tacoma, Washington.
Every December, the holiday boat parade kept her bridge up for one long hour.
Tanya hated that parade. So, of course, they put her in charge of it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SHORT STRAW
segments.quote: Our deeds determine us, as much as we determine our deeds.
segments.author: George Eliot
lines: The old organizer moved to Arizona, and her boss Gary handed Tanya a clipboard.
She grumbled all the way home. Her sister Renee was reading George Eliot, the English novelist.
Our deeds determine us, as much as we determine our deeds.
So Tanya decided to act like somebody who cared, and see what happened.
She bought a Santa hat.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FEUD
segments.quote: United we stand, divided we fall.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: Then came the meeting. The yacht club wanted to lead. The crab boat guys wanted to lead.
Somebody threw a donut. Nobody admitted it.
On the wall of the union hall hung an old line from Aesop:
United we stand, divided we fall.
So Tanya paired them up. One shiny yacht, one crab boat, side by side, every row.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: LIGHTS OUT
segments.quote: The great thing in this world is not so much where we stand, as in what direction we are moving.
segments.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.
lines: At the rehearsal, half the lights blew out. Two boats drifted into each other, gently, like an old married couple.
Tanya wanted to quit. An old tugboat captain named Walt read her a line from Oliver Wendell Holmes:
The great thing in this world is not so much where we stand, as in what direction we are moving.
So they kept moving. They rewired every boat by Friday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE STUCK BRIDGE
segments.quote: There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.
segments.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
lines: Parade night. Cold rain. Her bridge went up halfway, and stopped.
Everyone said the motor was dead.
Tanya thought of Sherlock Holmes, from Arthur Conan Doyle:
There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.
So she checked. A breaker had tripped behind the big wreath she had hung herself. One flip, and up it went.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: COCOA
segments.quote: Christmas is a season for kindling the fire of hospitality in the hall, the genial flame of charity in the heart.
segments.author: Washington Irving
lines: Now the crowd was wet and grumpy.
Renee texted her a line from Washington Irving, the American writer:
Christmas is a season for kindling the fire of hospitality in the hall, the genial flame of charity in the heart.
So Tanya opened the bridge office and made cocoa. Forty cups. Then sixty.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LAST BOAT
segments.quote: Happiness is not a goal; it is a by-product.
segments.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
lines: The boats sailed past, glowing, and the whole bridge cheered.
Tanya hadn't tried to be happy. She'd been too busy.
Walt raised his cup and quoted Eleanor Roosevelt:
Happiness is not a goal; it is a by-product.
The next year, Tanya didn't wait for anyone to ask. She signed up first.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Act first. Stand together. Keep moving. Check the facts. Open the door. Let joy follow.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Act like you care. Stand together. Keep moving. Check the obvious. Open the door. Let the joy follow.
I wore a Santa hat once. A dog followed me for three blocks, and I've never been prouder.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
